title: Slow androgenetic hair loss and produce regrowth with approved medicines

concept.text: Modify common pattern hair loss pharmacologically, increasing or maintaining visible scalp hair during treatment. Finasteride and topical minoxidil established this capability; they do not create a new supply of follicles. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for androgenetic alopecia supported by controlled human trials showing improved target-area hair counts and photographic or patient assessments over approximately one year. Test set by: FDA; Propecia's pivotal programme used hair counts, standardized photographs and patient/investigator assessments. Reported achieved: FDA approved finasteride 1 mg (Propecia) for male pattern hair loss on 19 December 1997; topical minoxidil was already an established treatment. Sources given: [FDA confirmation of Propecia approval date](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/human-drug-compounding/fda-alerts-health-care-providers-compounders-and-consumers-potential-risks-associated-compounded) ; [Propecia clinical evidence and prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=9e7329eb-39f1-4f84-a0bb-91daffaba1c3&type=display) ; [Topical minoxidil women's hair-regrowth label](https://dailymed.awsprod.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=c3ba93d7-e826-f6ac-e053-2a95a90a7951).

page.title: First FDA-approved medicines for androgenetic alopecia
page.definition: Androgenetic alopecia is progressive scalp hair loss in a characteristic pattern, commonly affecting the temples and crown in men and widening the central part in women. The first FDA-approved medicine for both populations was 2% minoxidil solution applied to the scalp, approved for men in 1988 and for women in 1991. FDA later approved oral finasteride 1 mg for male pattern hair loss in 1997.

goal.need: Pattern hair loss affects an estimated 50 million men and 30 million women in the United States. Wigs and concealers can hide thinning. Medicines can help people keep more of their own hair and sometimes regrow it. In two trials in men with thinning at the crown, 14% taking finasteride lost hair in the measured scalp area over 12 months, compared with 58% taking placebo. People who benefit from topical minoxidil need to keep using it to maintain the gain.

statements.quote: Patients are looking for effective hair loss treatments to prevent further thinning and optimally stimulate regrowth.
Treatment can prevent hair loss from worsening and help women regrow their hair.
statements.context: The passage concerns female pattern hair loss.

completion.title: FDA approves the first medicine for pattern hair loss in each clinical population.
completion.criterion: For each population, the test is met on the date FDA first approves a new drug application or an efficacy supplement whose approved labeling covers treatment of male pattern hair loss in men or female pattern hair loss in women, respectively. The two populations may qualify under the same drug application on different dates.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.105 and 314.71(c), governing approval of new drug applications and supplements.
completion.threshold_quote: the drug meets the statutory standards for safety and effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling
completion.basis: FDA determines what evidence establishes safety and effectiveness for the proposed use. Target-area hair counts are evidence for that decision. FDA identifies 2% topical minoxidil as the first approved treatment for both populations. Drugs@FDA records the original approval of NDA 019501 on August 17, 1988, for men and the new-indication approval under supplement 003 on August 13, 1991, for women.

milestones.title: Nonclinical evidence supports reasonably safe human testing of a candidate hair-loss medicine.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology information from laboratory animals or in vitro studies supports the sponsor's conclusion that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe. The kind, duration and scope of testing depend on the nature and duration of that investigation. Relevant existing studies may supply the evidence.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), the pharmacology and toxicology requirement for an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: the sponsor has concluded that it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: A candidate hair-loss medicine reaches human administration in clinical research.
milestones.criterion: People receive the candidate medicine under clinical monitoring to study its actions in humans, such as absorption after scalp application, or the side effects of the administered dose. Participants may be healthy volunteers or patients. For a population-specific result, the study documents exposure in that population.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, initial human testing under Phase I Clinical Studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans

milestones.title: Controlled studies provide preliminary evidence that a medicine treats pattern hair loss.
milestones.criterion: A controlled clinical study in patients with the relevant pattern of hair loss provides preliminary evidence that treatment slows further loss or promotes regrowth compared with the control and assesses common short-term adverse effects. Hair counts and standardized scalp photographs are examples of measures that can show a treatment effect.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c), controlled efficacy studies and the prerequisite for expanded clinical trials.
milestones.threshold_quote: preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

milestones.title: Expanded trials establish a medicine's benefit–risk profile for treating pattern hair loss.
milestones.criterion: After preliminary evidence of effectiveness, expanded clinical trials in the relevant population provide enough additional evidence on hair loss or regrowth and adverse effects to evaluate the medicine's overall benefits and risks and support prescribing information. Controlled comparisons can establish efficacy, and longer follow-up can contribute evidence on safety and persistence of benefit.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase 3 Clinical Studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship of the drug

milestones.title: A candidate medicine shows an effect on hair growth in a laboratory model of pattern hair loss.
milestones.criterion: An in vitro or animal experiment demonstrates an effect relevant to treating pattern hair loss, such as preservation of terminal hairs or regrowth from thinning follicles. The experiment identifies the model, treatment and observed hair or follicle response.
milestones.set_by: FDA, ICH M3(R2), section II, on primary pharmacodynamic studies during drug discovery.
milestones.threshold_quote: investigate the mode of action and/or effects of a substance in relation to its desired therapeutic target

milestones.title: FDA files the application for the pattern hair loss indication for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA files a new drug application or efficacy supplement seeking a pattern hair loss indication in the relevant population after determining that the submission is sufficiently complete for substantive review.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 314.101(a) and 314.71(c), in the New Drug and Antibiotic Regulations in force for the first approvals.
milestones.threshold_quote: the application is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

not_found: No FDA or society document located specified a universal minimum hair-count gain or a mandatory one-year trial for androgenetic alopecia medicines.
The original minoxidil hair-loss IND clearance and its complete supporting toxicology package were not located.

results.finding: Minoxidil in rats (sample size unreported) reduced fertility measures at oral doses of at least 3 mg/kg/day.
results.detail: Section 5.3 summarizes preclinical safety for the marketed product. It gives no proposed human study for which the sponsor assessed these data.
results.quote: Preclinical fertility studies in rats have shown minoxidil doses equal or greater than 3 mg/kg/day (at least 8 fold human exposure) when administered orally and greater than 9 mg/kg (at least 25-fold human exposure) administered subcutaneously in rats were associated with reduced conception and implantation rates

results.finding: Women received topical minoxidil in a pharmacokinetic study (sample size unreported). Once-daily 5% foam produced a similar AUC to the solution comparator.
results.detail: The female pharmacokinetic comparison gives no numerical AUC or participant count. The 322 participants belong to the separate efficacy trial.
results.quote: The AUC of 5% minoxidil foam used once daily was found to be similar to that of 2% minoxidil solution used twice daily in female subjects.

results.finding: Once-daily minoxidil foam in 397 women produced 9.1 more non-vellus hairs/cm² than vehicle at week 24.
results.detail: The source supplies expanded-trial efficacy and a broader safety summary. It gives no separate preliminary study with both controlled regrowth and short-term adverse-effect findings.
results.quote:
After 24 weeks of treatment, the 5% MTF OD group re-grew 13.4 hairs/cm
2
and the foam vehicle group re-grew 4.3 hairs/cm
2
, a treatment difference of 9.1 hairs/cm
2
(p<0.0001).

results.finding: Across two phase 3 trials in 719 women, once-daily minoxidil foam showed a 9.1 hairs/cm² advantage over vehicle in the placebo-controlled trial.
results.detail: Week-52 scalp coverage was a secondary observation. The adverse-reaction summary draws on trials of multiple topical formulations and postmarketing experience.
results.quote: The 2 efficacy studies demonstrated that 5% MTF OD provided benefits to women with FPHL after 12-24 weeks of treatment, including promotion of hair regrowth, improvement in scalp coverage, increase in hair density and hair diameter.

results.finding: Twenty-five women with female androgenetic alopecia received 3% topical minoxidil in a clinical study.
results.quote: To investigate the usefulness of topical minoxidil therapy in female androgenetic alopecia, we studied the efficacy and safety of 3% topical minoxidil in 25 affected women.

results.finding: 126 men with early male pattern baldness completed a 12-month trial in which all groups received topical minoxidil.
results.quote: One-hundred twenty-six healthy men with early male pattern baldness completed a 12-month double-blind, controlled trial of 2% and 3% topical minoxidil.

results.finding: In a trial with 126 male completers, topical minoxidil significantly increased vertex terminal hair growth versus placebo at 4 months.
results.detail: The text gives neither the magnitude of the between-group difference nor an exact p-value.
results.quote: Treatment of subjects with topical minoxidil for 4 months resulted in a statistically significant increase in terminal hair growth in comparison with placebo therapy.

results.finding: In a trial of 28 women with androgenetic alopecia, the active arm received 2% topical minoxidil.
results.detail: The excerpt gives the total study population. The number assigned to minoxidil is unspecified.
results.quote: Twenty-eight women with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia were randomly assigned to apply either 2 percent topical minoxidil or placebo (vehicle) to their involved scalp areas twice daily.

results.finding: In 28 women with androgenetic alopecia, topical minoxidil increased nonvellus target-area hair counts versus vehicle (p = 0.006).
results.quote: At the end of thirty-two weeks, there was a statistically significant increase of nonvellus target area hairs in the minoxidil-treated versus the vehicle-treated group (p = 0.006).

results.finding: In a trial of 113 women with androgenetic alopecia, 12.5% of the minoxidil foam group reported hair shedding.
results.detail: The foam and solution delivered 50 mg and 40 mg of minoxidil per day, respectively.
results.quote:
Hair shedding occurred in 17.5% of all
participants in the 2% MTS group compared with
12.5% in the 5% MTF population.

results.finding: In 113 women with androgenetic alopecia, once-daily minoxidil foam met the hair-count noninferiority margin of 7.5 hairs/cm² versus twice-daily solution.
results.detail: The trial used a single site and blinded investigators. Participants knew their assigned formulation. Follow-up ended at 24 weeks.
results.quote:
With a margin of noninferiority
of 7.5 hairs/cm2 a significant noninferiority of the 5%
MTF could be determined.

results.finding: Of 1,553 men with male pattern hair loss, 779 received oral finasteride under clinical monitoring.
results.quote:
In two 1-year trials, 1553 men (18 to 41 years of age) with male pattern hair loss
received oral finasteride 1 mg/d or placebo

results.finding: In phase III trials of 1,553 men with male pattern hair loss, finasteride produced 107 more vertex hairs than placebo at one year.
results.quote:
a difference of 107 ± 4.4 hairs (14%
± 0.6%) between groups (all P values < .001).

results.finding: Among 1,215 male extension participants, continued finasteride yielded a 138-hair vertex advantage over continued placebo at two years.
results.detail: The two-year hair-count contrast compared the groups assigned to continue their original treatments. The extension also included groups that switched treatments.
results.quote:
The difference between groups ( P < .001)
was 138 ± 16 hairs (16% ± 2.1%)

results.finding: Finasteride produced sustained scalp hair improvement versus placebo over five years in trials that randomized 1,553 men with male pattern hair loss.
results.detail: The 1,215 extension participants continued for up to four additional years. The excerpt gives no year-five sample size.
results.quote: Treatment with finasteride led to durable improvements in scalp hair over five years (p 3/4 0.001 versus placebo, all endpoints), while treatment with placebo led to progressive hair loss.

results.finding: Among 381 women in the monitored trial, the 5% topical minoxidil group averaged 1.8 ng/mL serum minoxidil after treatment.
results.quote:
The mean serum minoxidil level for all posttreat-
ment samples in the 5% topical minoxidil group was
1.8 ng/mL, which was 2.6 times higher than the level
seen in the 2% topical minoxidil group (0.7 ng/mL).

results.finding: In a trial of 381 women, 5% topical minoxidil increased nonvellus hair count by 10.6 hairs/cm² more than vehicle at week 8.
results.detail: The difference is calculated from the week-8 mean changes in Table IV. The 381 is the enrolled sample. Hair-count analyses used the efficacy-evaluable population.
results.quote:
In addition, the mean change in target area
nonvellus hair counts in the 5% and 2% topical
minoxidil groups was signi ﬁcantly superior to the
placebo group beginning at week 8 and continuing
throughout the trial (Table IV, Fig 2).

results.finding: In the 381-woman minoxidil trial, 14% of the 5% group experienced a drug-related dermatologic adverse event.
results.detail: About 30% of participants discontinued across the trial arms. The full efficacy-evaluable analysis found no significant hair-count difference between the two active concentrations at week 48.
results.quote:
Drug-related adverse events of
a dermatologic nature (eg, pruritus, dermatitis, hy-
pertrichosis, scaling) were more prevalent in the 5%
topical minoxidil group (22 of 153 patients; 14%)
than in the 2% topical minoxidil group (10 of 154
patients; 6%) and the placebo group (3 of 74 pa-
tients; 4%).

results.finding: In 18 stump-tailed macaques, topical minoxidil enlarged vellus follicles in frontal bald scalp to intermediate or terminal size.
results.detail: Regrowth was more prominent in younger macaques with early baldness than in older animals with longer-standing baldness.
results.quote: minoxidil induces the enlargement of vellus follicles to the size of middle to terminal follicles (regrowth of hair effect)

results.finding: Finasteride showed no tumorigenic effect in male rats at up to 888 times human exposure. Sample size unreported.
results.detail: Section 13.1 also reports genotoxicity and fertility studies. The label does not tie the nonclinical package to a proposed human investigation.
results.quote:
No evidence of a tumorigenic effect was observed in a 24-month study in Sprague-Dawley rats receiving doses of 
finasteride up to 160 mg/kg/day in males and 320 mg/kg/day in females.

results.finding: Prenatal finasteride exposure caused hypospadias in up to 100% of male rat offspring. Sample size unreported.
results.detail: The label uses these data to explain the pregnancy contraindication. It does not describe the nonclinical basis for proceeding with the postmenopausal trial.
results.quote:
there was a dose-
dependent increase in hypospadias th at occurred in 3.6 to 100% of male offspring.

results.finding: In controlled male pattern hair loss trials, 1.4% of finasteride recipients (n=945) discontinued because of potentially drug-related adverse experiences.
results.quote:
In three controlled clinical trials for PROPECIA of 12-month duration, 1.4% of patients taking PROPECIA (n=945) 
were discontinued due to adve rse experiences that were considered to be possibly, probably or definitely drug-
related (1.6% for placebo; n=934).

results.finding: In a monitored trial of postmenopausal women with pattern hair loss (n=137), 67 received finasteride.
results.quote:
In a study involving 137 postmenopausal women with androgenetic alopecia who were treated with PROPECIA 
(n=67) or placebo (n=70) for 12 months, effectiveness c ould not be demonstrated.

results.finding: At 12 months, men with vertex hair loss (n=1,351 analyzed) taking finasteride had 107 more hairs in the target area than men taking placebo.
results.detail: Men in both arms used a specified tar-based shampoo. Sexual function questionnaires assessed effects such as changes in sexual interest and erections.
results.quote:
At 12 months there was a 107-hair difference from placebo (p<0. 001, PROPECIA [n =679] vs placebo 
[n=672]) within a 1-inch diameter circle (5.1 cm 2).

results.finding: In postmenopausal women with pattern hair loss (n=137), finasteride showed no hair-count benefit over placebo at 12 months.
results.quote:
In a study involving 137 postmenopausal women with androgenetic alopecia who were treated with PROPECIA 
(n=67) or placebo (n=70) for 12 months, effectiveness c ould not be demonstrated.

results.finding: At five years, men with vertex hair loss (n=234 analyzed) taking finasteride had 277 more hairs in the target area than men taking placebo.
results.detail: Only 15 placebo recipients contributed to the five-year hair-count comparison. Men switched from finasteride to placebo after year one lost the hair-count gain over the following year.
results.quote:
resulting in a 277-hair di fference (p<0.001, PROPECIA [n=219] vs placebo [n=15]) at 5 years (see 
Figure 1 below).

title = "First FDA-approved medicines for androgenetic alopecia". Reason: Naming FDA makes clear which jurisdiction determines both historical firsts.

definition = "Androgenetic alopecia is progressive scalp hair loss in a characteristic pattern, commonly affecting the temples and crown in men and widening the central part in women. The first FDA-approved medicine for both populations was 2% minoxidil solution applied to the scalp, approved for men in 1988 and for women in 1991. FDA later approved oral finasteride 1 mg for male pattern hair loss in 1997.". Reason: The definition gives finasteride apparent joint priority and makes a particular hair-count endpoint part of the meaning of approval.

goal.need = "Pattern hair loss affects an estimated 50 million men and 30 million women in the United States. Wigs and concealers can hide thinning. Medicines can help people keep more of their own hair and sometimes regrow it. In two trials in men with thinning at the crown, 14% taking finasteride lost hair in the measured scalp area over 12 months, compared with 58% taking placebo. People who benefit from topical minoxidil need to keep using it to maintain the gain.". Reason: The current paragraph points to absent prevalence figures and gives the placebo outcome without explaining how much treatment changed it.

The two populations may qualify under the same drug application on different dates."; set_by = "U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.105 and 314.71(c), governing approval of new drug applications and supplements."; set_by_kind = "regulator"; threshold_quote = "the drug meets the statutory standards for safety and effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling"; threshold_ref = 5; basis = "FDA determines what evidence establishes safety and effectiveness for the proposed use. add milestone after None: "A candidate medicine shows an effect on hair growth in a laboratory model of pattern hair loss.". Reason: A laboratory demonstration that a drug affects hair growth is a distinct result that the current safety milestone can record only as partial.

The kind, duration and scope of testing depend on the nature and duration of that investigation. Relevant existing studies may supply the evidence."; threshold_quote = "the sponsor has concluded that it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations."; threshold_ref = 9; refs = [9, 11]. edit m2: criterion = "People receive the candidate medicine under clinical monitoring to study its actions in humans, such as absorption after scalp application, or the side effects of the administered dose. edit m3: criterion = "A controlled clinical study in patients with the relevant pattern of hair loss provides preliminary evidence that treatment slows further loss or promotes regrowth compared with the control and assesses common short-term adverse effects. Hair counts and standardized scalp photographs are examples of measures that can show a treatment effect."; threshold_quote = "preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained"; threshold_ref = 14; refs = [14, 3]. Reason: The phase 2 rule calls for controlled evidence of effectiveness and short-term risks without specifying a hair-count endpoint or P < 0.05.
